From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**HEY** is a [premium email](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium_email "Premium email") service launched by [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") in June 2020.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-4)

The service may be accessed through the HEY website and through apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6) Due to the service's [vertical integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertical_integration "Vertical integration"), a HEY [mailbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_box "Email box") cannot be incorporated into other email services or stand-alone [email clients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_client "Email client").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-7)

Around the time of HEY's launch, a stand-off between [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") and [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") over Apple's policy on [in-app purchases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtransaction "Microtransaction") in apps hosted by its [App Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/App_Store_(iOS) "App Store (iOS)") was the cause of significant media attention upon Apple's policies.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-11)

*   An email from a new sender requires the user to confirm whether they wish to receive emails from that sender, and if not then emails from that sender are never shown again[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   Blocks [tracking pixels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracking_pixel "Tracking pixel") (called a spy tracker in the apps) and informs the user if an email includes tracking[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   A single place showing all attachments that have been received, regardless of sender[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)

*   [Mailbox provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailbox_provider "Mailbox provider")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**HEY** is a [premium email](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium_email "Premium email") service launched by [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") in June 2020.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-4)

The service may be accessed through the HEY website and through apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6) Due to the service's [vertical integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertical_integration "Vertical integration"), a HEY [mailbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_box "Email box") cannot be incorporated into other email services or stand-alone [email clients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_client "Email client").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-7)

Around the time of HEY's launch, a stand-off between [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") and [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") over Apple's policy on [in-app purchases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtransaction "Microtransaction") in apps hosted by its [App Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/App_Store_(iOS) "App Store (iOS)") was the cause of significant media attention upon Apple's policies.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-11)

*   An email from a new sender requires the user to confirm whether they wish to receive emails from that sender, and if not then emails from that sender are never shown again[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   Blocks [tracking pixels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracking_pixel "Tracking pixel") (called a spy tracker in the apps) and informs the user if an email includes tracking[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   A single place showing all attachments that have been received, regardless of sender[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)

*   [Mailbox provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailbox_provider "Mailbox provider")

[hey]/ heɪ /

## interjection

hey _British_

/ heɪ /

## interjection

1.   an expression indicating surprise, dismay, discovery, etc, or calling for another's attention

2.   an exclamation used for emphasis at the end of a statement, or alone to seek repetition or confirmation of another person's statement

3.   an exclamation used by conjurors to herald the climax of a trick

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**HEY** is a [premium email](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium_email "Premium email") service launched by [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") in June 2020.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-4)

The service may be accessed through the HEY website and through apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6) Due to the service's [vertical integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertical_integration "Vertical integration"), a HEY [mailbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_box "Email box") cannot be incorporated into other email services or stand-alone [email clients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_client "Email client").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-7)

Around the time of HEY's launch, a stand-off between [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") and [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") over Apple's policy on [in-app purchases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtransaction "Microtransaction") in apps hosted by its [App Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/App_Store_(iOS) "App Store (iOS)") was the cause of significant media attention upon Apple's policies.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-11)

*   An email from a new sender requires the user to confirm whether they wish to receive emails from that sender, and if not then emails from that sender are never shown again[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   Blocks [tracking pixels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracking_pixel "Tracking pixel") (called a spy tracker in the apps) and informs the user if an email includes tracking[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   A single place showing all attachments that have been received, regardless of sender[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)

*   [Mailbox provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailbox_provider "Mailbox provider")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**HEY** is a [premium email](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium_email "Premium email") service launched by [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") in June 2020.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-4)

The service may be accessed through the HEY website and through apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6) Due to the service's [vertical integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertical_integration "Vertical integration"), a HEY [mailbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_box "Email box") cannot be incorporated into other email services or stand-alone [email clients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_client "Email client").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-7)

Around the time of HEY's launch, a stand-off between [37signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37signals "37signals") and [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") over Apple's policy on [in-app purchases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtransaction "Microtransaction") in apps hosted by its [App Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/App_Store_(iOS) "App Store (iOS)") was the cause of significant media attention upon Apple's policies.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-11)

*   An email from a new sender requires the user to confirm whether they wish to receive emails from that sender, and if not then emails from that sender are never shown again[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   Blocks [tracking pixels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracking_pixel "Tracking pixel") (called a spy tracker in the apps) and informs the user if an email includes tracking[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)
*   A single place showing all attachments that have been received, regardless of sender[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_(email_service)#cite_note-inc-aten-6)

*   [Mailbox provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailbox_provider "Mailbox provider")
